transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is my thinking feels… off. Like my head is foggy, and I’m not usually like that. I work as a personal care aide, so I’m used to keeping track of details and writing things down clearly, but lately I’ve been making these little mistakes in my client notes—nothing huge, I don’t think, but enough that I notice it and it bothers me.

And I’ll start to do something, like I’m in the middle of a task, and then I just kind of blank on what I was about to do. It’s frustrating because I’m 43, I know my routines, I know my work, and I’m usually pretty on top of things. But now it feels like I’m moving through the day with this haze in my head, and I don’t trust myself as much with the small stuff. That’s what made me think I should come in and talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’ve still been getting up and going to work, and I can talk to my clients and do what I’m supposed to do, so from the outside I probably seem okay. But inside it’s been different.

Lately when I wake up, there’s this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It’s not even always like I’m crying or anything dramatic, it’s more like this sad, flat feeling that’s just sitting there. I can push through my shift and answer people and make small talk, but it feels like I’m kind of doing it from behind a wall, if that makes sense. Like I’m present, but inside I’m just… low. Sad and kind of hollow.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I don’t think I’ve noticed some big thing where I suddenly hate everything I used to like. It’s more that when I do things, I’m kind of not fully in them, if that makes sense.

Like, I’ll still put on a show or scroll on my phone or talk to someone if they call, but I don’t always get much out of it. But I also don’t know if that’s “losing interest” or just being tired or distracted or in my own head. I haven’t really sat down and thought, “Oh, I don’t enjoy anything anymore.” It’s more… I don’t know. Things feel a little muted, maybe. But I wouldn’t want to overstate it.
How have you been sleeping lately?

Not great, honestly. It’s been kind of all over the place. Some nights I get into bed and I’m tired, like I know I should be able to sleep, but then my mind just starts going. A lot of it is family stuff—little things, worries, conversations, what I should’ve done or what I need to do—and I’ll just lie there staring into the dark, kind of turning it over and over.

And then other mornings I wake up before my alarm, not even for a clear reason, and once I’m awake I can’t really settle back down. I’ll try to tell myself, “You still have time, just go back to sleep,” but it doesn’t happen. I end up just lying there half-resting, half-thinking, and by the time I actually need to get up I already feel like I’ve been awake for a while. So yeah, it’s not like one simple pattern, but it hasn’t felt steady.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?

I don’t know if I’d say “a lot” exactly. I mean, I do get stuck thinking about things sometimes, especially when I’m trying to settle down, but it’s hard for me to separate what’s normal worrying from something more than that.

It’s not like I’m walking around every minute panicking or imagining disasters, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like my mind picks up little things and keeps turning them over—stuff I said, things I need to do, whether I handled something right. But I don’t know… I wouldn’t want to make it sound bigger than it is. It’s there, but I’m not sure how much counts as “a lot.”
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I’m collapsing or anything, but I do feel more worn out than I’d expect. Even on days where I haven’t really done that much, my body can feel like I’ve been going all day.

Like with work, helping a client shower or doing the usual care stuff, things I normally can handle, it just feels like it takes more out of me. And even simple things outside of work, like carrying groceries in, I’ll notice I’m more drained than I think I should be. It’s kind of frustrating because I’ll think, “I didn’t even do enough to feel this tired,” but my body doesn’t seem to agree.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I’d say it really started, or at least became noticeable, after my uncle died… so about two weeks ago now. Before that, I mean, I had normal tired days here and there like anybody, but this whole shift in how I’ve been feeling, the being worn down and not quite sleeping right, it kind of started around then. It’s been hard to tell because the days have sort of blended together a little since it happened, but when I think back, that’s the point where I noticed I wasn’t feeling like myself.
Since your uncle died, have you found yourself strongly longing for him or preoccupied with thoughts about him?

I don’t know if I’d call it “strongly longing,” exactly. I mean, I think about him, sure. It comes up, especially if something reminds me of him, or if there’s a quiet moment and my mind wanders that way. But I’m not sitting there all day just focused on him, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more like… it’s there in the background sometimes. I’ll remember something about him or think, “Wow, he’s really gone,” and that feels strange. But I don’t know that I’d say I’m preoccupied. At least not in a way where I can’t think about anything else.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?

Yeah… guilty, definitely. Worthless, I don’t know if I’d use that exact word, but I’ve been feeling like I let him down. My tío, I mean.

I keep going back over it in my head, like, “Why didn’t I call him more?” or “Why did I keep putting off visiting?” And I know people say you can’t think like that, you don’t always know what’s going to happen, but it doesn’t really stop my brain from doing it. I’ll remember times I thought about reaching out and then got busy or tired or said, “I’ll do it later,” and now there isn’t a later. That part really gets to me.

It’s like I failed him as family somehow. Like I should’ve been more present, checked in more, made more effort before he died. I don’t know if that’s fair, but it’s where my mind keeps going.
Has this been making it hard for you to function at work or take care of things at home?

Yeah… somewhat. I mean, I’m still showing up and doing what I’m supposed to do, so it’s not like everything has completely fallen apart, but I can tell I’m not as sharp with the little details.

At work, because I do care work, there’s paperwork and notes for clients, and usually I’m pretty careful with that. Lately I’ve been second-guessing myself more, like, “Did I write that down right? Did I miss something?” So I’ve had to ask coworkers to look over my documentation, just to make sure I didn’t mess anything up. That’s embarrassing for me, honestly, because I don’t like feeling like people have to babysit my work.

And at home, my wife has picked up some of the bills and scheduling stuff, like appointments or things we need to keep track of. Normally I can manage my share of that, but right now I’m just not as reliable with details. I’ll forget to follow through or I’ll sit there staring at something and not really process it. So yeah, it’s affecting things, not severely, but enough that other people are having to compensate for me.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

I’m not planning to hurt myself. I want to say that clearly, because even saying this out loud makes me nervous, like I don’t want anyone to think I’m about to do something.

But… there have been mornings where I wake up and, before I even really get going, I have this thought like, “If I just hadn’t woken up today, maybe that wouldn’t have been the worst thing.” Not like I’m making a plan or thinking through how to hurt myself. It’s more passive than that, I guess. Like being tired of feeling the way I’m feeling, and then that thought shows up.

And honestly, it scares me. Because I don’t usually think like that, and then I feel guilty or ashamed for even having the thought. I haven’t done anything to harm myself, and I’m not sitting there planning it, but yeah… those thoughts have crossed my mind.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt this sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. Most days, anyway. It’s been this thing where I wake up and before anything has even happened, there’s already this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I haven’t even gotten out of bed yet and it’s just… there.

I can still go to work, I can talk to people, do my shift, answer questions, whatever I need to do on the outside. So I don’t think everyone would necessarily look at me and say, “Oh, he’s sad all day.” But inside I feel really flat. Like I’m moving through the day, but there’s not much there underneath except this sadness.

And it’s not every single second, I guess. If someone talks to me, I can respond, maybe even laugh a little if I’m supposed to. But then when things get quiet again, it drops right back down. So yeah… over the past couple weeks, it’s been most of the day, nearly every day.
Have you noticed your appetite has gone down lately?

I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed it going down, like I’m not looking at meals and feeling repulsed by food or anything like that.

Some days I don’t feel especially interested in eating, but I can’t tell if that’s an appetite thing or just me being distracted and not thinking about it until later. If food is in front of me, I usually eat. I haven’t been tracking it closely, though, so I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually one of the main things that made me think, okay, maybe I need to talk to someone, because my head has just felt foggy lately.

It’s not like I can’t understand things, exactly. It’s more like I’ll be in the middle of doing something and then suddenly I forget what I was about to do. Or I’ll read something and have to go back over it because it didn’t really stick the first time. And with my work, that worries me, because I’m usually pretty careful. I’ve been making these little mistakes in my client notes — nothing huge, but enough that I notice, like leaving something out or having to double-check myself because I’m not sure if I wrote it down right.

That’s not really like me. I take that stuff seriously. So when I catch myself blanking out or losing my train of thought, it makes me feel even worse, because then I start thinking, “What is wrong with me? Why can’t I just focus?” It’s been frustrating.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, no. I mean… I feel slower inside, if that makes sense, like it takes me longer to get myself going or to sort through what I’m trying to do, but I’m not sure other people would say I’m moving slowly or talking slowly.

At work I’m still doing my normal tasks, walking around, helping people, answering questions. I haven’t had anyone ask me if I’m okay because I’m speaking weird or moving like I’m in slow motion or anything like that. Maybe I pause more because I’m trying to gather my thoughts, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as actually being slowed down.

So… not noticeably, I guess. Not that I can clearly point to.
Over the past two weeks, have you found little or no pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I wouldn’t say I have little or no pleasure in everything. It’s not like nothing feels good or I can’t enjoy anything at all.

There have been times where I don’t feel as interested in doing things, or I sort of go through the motions, but I don’t know if that’s the same as not getting pleasure from things. Like, if I watch something I like or spend time doing something familiar, I can still enjoy parts of it. It just maybe doesn’t always pull me in the way it normally would.

But I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really sat there thinking, “I don’t enjoy anything anymore.” It’s more unclear than that. So… I guess I’d say not clearly, or not to the point where I’d call it little or no pleasure.
Since your uncle died, have there still been moments when something good happens and your mood genuinely lifts, even briefly?

Yeah… I mean, yes, there are still moments where something good happens and I can feel myself lift a little. It’s not like I’m completely unreachable or nothing can touch me.

But lately, the bigger thing is that I keep waking up with this heaviness, like right in my chest. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it feels sort of empty and weighted at the same time. I can get up, I can go to work, I can do my shift, I can talk to people and answer them normally enough, and I don’t think most people would necessarily know what’s going on inside. But underneath it, I just feel sad and flat.

So if something nice happens, sure, I might laugh for a second or feel a little better briefly. But it doesn’t really last. It’s like the good moment passes, and then I’m right back to that heavy feeling again.
Have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic or driven, more than your normal self?

Yeah… there was a stretch like that. I don’t know if I’d call it “energetic” in a good way, exactly, but I was definitely more driven than usual. Like I couldn’t sit still.

It was almost like if I stopped moving, all the grief would catch up to me, so I just kept finding things to do. Errands that probably didn’t need to be done right then, little chores around the house, making calls, checking on things, organizing stuff, going back out for one more thing even if I’d already been out. I’d tell myself I was just being useful or staying on top of things, but honestly it felt more like I was trying to outrun something.

I remember feeling kind of restless, like sitting down made me uncomfortable, not physically exactly, but emotionally. If I was still for too long, my mind would go right back to everything, so I’d pop up and do another task. It wasn’t really like my normal pace. I’m usually busy with work and regular responsibilities, but this felt more urgent, like I had to keep moving.
During that driven, restless stretch, did you need less sleep than usual?

Yeah… during that stretch, I did sleep less. Not every single night maybe, but for several nights I was only getting, I don’t know, maybe three or four hours.

The strange part was that I didn’t wake up feeling wrecked the way I normally would if I got that little sleep. I’d get up and feel kind of charged, like I was already switched on. I’d still make coffee, but honestly it was more because that’s just what I do in the morning than because I felt like I needed it to function.

It stood out to me because normally if I only sleep a few hours, I feel it. I drag. But then I was just up and going, like my body had decided we were starting the day whether it made sense or not.
During that period when you were sleeping only a few hours and still felt charged, did you feel more confident or capable than usual?

Yeah… I did. At the time it didn’t feel like “confidence” exactly, it felt more like clarity, like I suddenly saw the whole path laid out and everyone else was just moving too slowly.

I got really convinced that I didn’t need to keep waiting or planning or second-guessing myself. I was thinking, why am I just working as an aide for other people when I already know the work, I know what families need, I know how many Spanish-speaking seniors and families struggle to find the right help. And in my head it became this whole thing — like I could start a Spanish-speaking senior-care agency right away.

And I don’t mean just as a vague dream, like “maybe someday.” I mean I honestly believed I had it figured out. Like I could put the pieces together immediately and it would work because… I don’t know, because it made sense to me. I felt like I couldn’t really fail at it. Looking back, that part feels a little embarrassing to say out loud, because starting an agency is not some small thing. But during that stretch, it felt obvious, like I was capable of handling all of it and everybody else would eventually see that too.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the symptoms are occurring in the context of bereavement with prominent grief-related yearning, which would help distinguish adjustment disorder from a major depressive episode or primary anxiety/insomnia problem.
doctor.question: Since your uncle died, have you found yourself strongly longing for him or preoccupied with thoughts about him?

target_item.reason: The question is about grief-related longing or preoccupation with thoughts of the uncle, which is not directly covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it “strongly longing,” exactly. I mean, I think about him, sure. It comes up, especially if something reminds me of him, or if there’s a quiet moment and my mind wanders that way. But I’m not sitting there all day just focused on him, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more like… it’s there in the background sometimes. I’ll remember something about him or think, “Wow, he’s really gone,” and that feels strange. But I don’t know that I’d say I’m preoccupied. At least not in a way where I can’t think about anything else.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has been feeling worthless or excessively guilty, which would help distinguish a depressive episode from normal grief/adjustment-related symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep replaying what I should have done for my tío before he died, like calling more or visiting sooner, and I end up feeling like I failed him as family.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question directly asks about feelings of worthlessness or guilt lately.

patient.answer:
Yeah… guilty, definitely. Worthless, I don’t know if I’d use that exact word, but I’ve been feeling like I let him down. My tío, I mean.

I keep going back over it in my head, like, “Why didn’t I call him more?” or “Why did I keep putting off visiting?” And I know people say you can’t think like that, you don’t always know what’s going to happen, but it doesn’t really stop my brain from doing it. I’ll remember times I thought about reaching out and then got busy or tired or said, “I’ll do it later,” and now there isn’t a later. That part really gets to me.

It’s like I failed him as family somehow. Like I should’ve been more present, checked in more, made more effort before he died. I don’t know if that’s fair, but it’s where my mind keeps going.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the mood symptoms are impairing functioning enough to suggest a depressive episode rather than a normal grief reaction or isolated insomnia/anxiety.
doctor.question: Has this been making it hard for you to function at work or take care of things at home?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: At work I’ve had to ask coworkers to double-check my client documentation, and at home my wife has taken over some bills and scheduling because I’m not as reliable with details right now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms are interfering with work functioning or responsibilities at home, which directly matches the functional impairment profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… somewhat. I mean, I’m still showing up and doing what I’m supposed to do, so it’s not like everything has completely fallen apart, but I can tell I’m not as sharp with the little details.

At work, because I do care work, there’s paperwork and notes for clients, and usually I’m pretty careful with that. Lately I’ve been second-guessing myself more, like, “Did I write that down right? Did I miss something?” So I’ve had to ask coworkers to look over my documentation, just to make sure I didn’t mess anything up. That’s embarrassing for me, honestly, because I don’t like feeling like people have to babysit my work.

And at home, my wife has picked up some of the bills and scheduling stuff, like appointments or things we need to keep track of. Normally I can manage my share of that, but right now I’m just not as reliable with details. I’ll forget to follow through or I’ll sit there staring at something and not really process it. So yeah, it’s affecting things, not severely, but enough that other people are having to compensate for me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the symptoms represent a normal grief reaction/adjustment disorder versus a major depressive episode by assessing for suicidal ideation.
doctor.question: Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I’m not planning to hurt myself, but there have been mornings when I think it wouldn’t be the worst thing if I just didn’t wake up, and that scares me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about thoughts that life is not worth living or thoughts of self-harm, which corresponds to death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
I’m not planning to hurt myself. I want to say that clearly, because even saying this out loud makes me nervous, like I don’t want anyone to think I’m about to do something.

But… there have been mornings where I wake up and, before I even really get going, I have this thought like, “If I just hadn’t woken up today, maybe that wouldn’t have been the worst thing.” Not like I’m making a plan or thinking through how to hurt myself. It’s more passive than that, I guess. Like being tired of feeling the way I’m feeling, and then that thought shows up.

And honestly, it scares me. Because I don’t usually think like that, and then I feel guilty or ashamed for even having the thought. I haven’t done anything to harm myself, and I’m not sitting there planning it, but yeah… those thoughts have crossed my mind.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the low mood and other symptoms have been present most of the day nearly every day for the past two weeks, which best distinguishes a major depressive episode from a grief-related adjustment reaction at this point.
doctor.question: Over the past two weeks, have you felt this sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like I can get through my shift and talk to people but inside I’m just sad and flat.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about persistent sad or empty mood most of the day nearly every day over the past two weeks, which matches Depressed_Mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. Most days, anyway. It’s been this thing where I wake up and before anything has even happened, there’s already this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I haven’t even gotten out of bed yet and it’s just… there.

I can still go to work, I can talk to people, do my shift, answer questions, whatever I need to do on the outside. So I don’t think everyone would necessarily look at me and say, “Oh, he’s sad all day.” But inside I feel really flat. Like I’m moving through the day, but there’s not much there underneath except this sadness.

And it’s not every single second, I guess. If someone talks to me, I can respond, maybe even laugh a little if I’m supposed to. But then when things get quiet again, it drops right back down. So yeah… over the past couple weeks, it’s been most of the day, nearly every day.

inference.note: Current turn confirms depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for ~2 weeks, increasing support for a depressive episode; however onset immediately after bereavement keeps adjustment disorder with depressed mood in the differential. No change otherwise.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a meaningful decrease in appetite, which would help distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder or anxiety-related symptoms.
doctor.question: Have you noticed your appetite has gone down lately?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about decreased appetite, but the provided symptom profile does not include an appetite or weight-change symptom item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly noticed it going down, like I’m not looking at meals and feeling repulsed by food or anything like that.

Some days I don’t feel especially interested in eating, but I can’t tell if that’s an appetite thing or just me being distracted and not thinking about it until later. If food is in front of me, I usually eat. I haven’t been tracking it closely, though, so I don’t want to say yes if I’m not sure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has impaired concentration, which would help distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder or primary insomnia/anxiety and also clarify the cause of the reported memory problems.
doctor.question: Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my head feels foggy, and I’m making little mistakes in my client notes and forgetting what I was about to do, which isn’t like me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about trouble concentrating lately, which matches diminished ability to think or concentrate.

patient.answer:
Yeah… definitely. That’s actually one of the main things that made me think, okay, maybe I need to talk to someone, because my head has just felt foggy lately.

It’s not like I can’t understand things, exactly. It’s more like I’ll be in the middle of doing something and then suddenly I forget what I was about to do. Or I’ll read something and have to go back over it because it didn’t really stick the first time. And with my work, that worries me, because I’m usually pretty careful. I’ve been making these little mistakes in my client notes — nothing huge, but enough that I notice, like leaving something out or having to double-check myself because I’m not sure if I wrote it down right.

That’s not really like me. I take that stuff seriously. So when I catch myself blanking out or losing my train of thought, it makes me feel even worse, because then I start thinking, “What is wrong with me? Why can’t I just focus?” It’s been frustrating.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has had prominent psychomotor retardation, which would add another major depressive symptom and help distinguish a major depressive episode from adjustment disorder with depressed mood.
doctor.question: Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about psychomotor slowing, such as moving or speaking more slowly than usual, and the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for psychomotor retardation or observable slowing.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, no. I mean… I feel slower inside, if that makes sense, like it takes me longer to get myself going or to sort through what I’m trying to do, but I’m not sure other people would say I’m moving slowly or talking slowly.

At work I’m still doing my normal tasks, walking around, helping people, answering questions. I haven’t had anyone ask me if I’m okay because I’m speaking weird or moving like I’m in slow motion or anything like that. Maybe I pause more because I’m trying to gather my thoughts, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as actually being slowed down.

So… not noticeably, I guess. Not that I can clearly point to.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has experienced a clear loss of interest or pleasure, which would help distinguish a major depressive episode from grief-related adjustment symptoms.
doctor.question: Over the past two weeks, have you found little or no pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

target_item.reason: The question is directly about diminished interest or pleasure (anhedonia), but the provided symptom profile does not include an anhedonia item.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I wouldn’t say I have little or no pleasure in everything. It’s not like nothing feels good or I can’t enjoy anything at all.

There have been times where I don’t feel as interested in doing things, or I sort of go through the motions, but I don’t know if that’s the same as not getting pleasure from things. Like, if I watch something I like or spend time doing something familiar, I can still enjoy parts of it. It just maybe doesn’t always pull me in the way it normally would.

But I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really sat there thinking, “I don’t enjoy anything anymore.” It’s more unclear than that. So… I guess I’d say not clearly, or not to the point where I’d call it little or no pleasure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms are better explained by a normal/adjustment-related grief reaction versus a major depressive episode by assessing whether mood remains responsive to positive events.
doctor.question: Since your uncle died, have there still been moments when something good happens and your mood genuinely lifts, even briefly?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like I can get through my shift and talk to people but inside I’m just sad and flat.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient’s mood can brighten in response to positive events since the uncle’s death, which directly relates to the quality and persistence/reactivity of depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, yes, there are still moments where something good happens and I can feel myself lift a little. It’s not like I’m completely unreachable or nothing can touch me.

But lately, the bigger thing is that I keep waking up with this heaviness, like right in my chest. It’s hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it feels sort of empty and weighted at the same time. I can get up, I can go to work, I can do my shift, I can talk to people and answer them normally enough, and I don’t think most people would necessarily know what’s going on inside. But underneath it, I just feel sad and flat.

So if something nice happens, sure, I might laugh for a second or feel a little better briefly. But it doesn’t really last. It’s like the good moment passes, and then I’m right back to that heavy feeling again.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been any increase in goal-directed activity or abnormally elevated energy, to rule out a history of mania/hypomania before concluding a depressive diagnosis.
doctor.question: Have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic or driven, more than your normal self?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: During that time I couldn’t sit still, like if I stopped moving the grief would catch me, so I kept finding errands, calls, and chores to do.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a period of unusually increased energy or drive beyond the patient’s normal self, which directly matches increased activity or energy.

patient.answer:
Yeah… there was a stretch like that. I don’t know if I’d call it “energetic” in a good way, exactly, but I was definitely more driven than usual. Like I couldn’t sit still.

It was almost like if I stopped moving, all the grief would catch up to me, so I just kept finding things to do. Errands that probably didn’t need to be done right then, little chores around the house, making calls, checking on things, organizing stuff, going back out for one more thing even if I’d already been out. I’d tell myself I was just being useful or staying on top of things, but honestly it felt more like I was trying to outrun something.

I remember feeling kind of restless, like sitting down made me uncomfortable, not physically exactly, but emotionally. If I was still for too long, my mind would go right back to everything, so I’d pop up and do another task. It wasn’t really like my normal pace. I’m usually busy with work and regular responsibilities, but this felt more urgent, like I had to keep moving.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the recent driven/restless period involved decreased need for sleep, which would help distinguish a grief/depressive reaction from a bipolar-spectrum episode.
doctor.question: During that driven, restless stretch, did you need less sleep than usual?

target_item.name: Decreased_Sleep
target_item.manifestation: For several nights I slept maybe three or four hours and still got up feeling charged, making coffee more out of habit than because I felt tired.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether, during the driven/restless stretch, there was a reduced need for sleep compared with usual.

patient.answer:
Yeah… during that stretch, I did sleep less. Not every single night maybe, but for several nights I was only getting, I don’t know, maybe three or four hours.

The strange part was that I didn’t wake up feeling wrecked the way I normally would if I got that little sleep. I’d get up and feel kind of charged, like I was already switched on. I’d still make coffee, but honestly it was more because that’s just what I do in the morning than because I felt like I needed it to function.

It stood out to me because normally if I only sleep a few hours, I feel it. I drag. But then I was just up and going, like my body had decided we were starting the day whether it made sense or not.

inference.note: New history of a distinct restless/driven period with decreased need for sleep (3–4 hours without feeling tired) raises concern for bipolar spectrum disorder, so F31.9 is added. Pure sleep disorder and memory-symptom coding are less likely as primary diagnoses given mood syndrome context, so F51.9 and R41.3 are removed.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the decreased need for sleep/restless driven period was accompanied by elevated self-esteem or grandiosity, which would strongly support a hypomanic/manic episode over depression, adjustment disorder, or anxiety.
doctor.question: During that period when you were sleeping only a few hours and still felt charged, did you feel more confident or capable than usual?

target_item.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
target_item.manifestation: I honestly believed I could quit waiting around and start a Spanish-speaking senior-care agency right away, like I had everything figured out and couldn’t really fail.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether, during the energized low-sleep period, the patient felt unusually confident or capable, which directly maps to inflated self-esteem or grandiosity.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I did. At the time it didn’t feel like “confidence” exactly, it felt more like clarity, like I suddenly saw the whole path laid out and everyone else was just moving too slowly.

I got really convinced that I didn’t need to keep waiting or planning or second-guessing myself. I was thinking, why am I just working as an aide for other people when I already know the work, I know what families need, I know how many Spanish-speaking seniors and families struggle to find the right help. And in my head it became this whole thing — like I could start a Spanish-speaking senior-care agency right away.

And I don’t mean just as a vague dream, like “maybe someday.” I mean I honestly believed I had it figured out. Like I could put the pieces together immediately and it would work because… I don’t know, because it made sense to me. I felt like I couldn’t really fail at it. Looking back, that part feels a little embarrassing to say out loud, because starting an agency is not some small thing. But during that stretch, it felt obvious, like I was capable of handling all of it and everybody else would eventually see that too.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient currently has a depressive syndrome with sad/empty mood most of the day for nearly 2 weeks, insomnia, fatigue, guilt, impaired concentration, passive death wishes, and functional impairment. Critically, he also reports a distinct prior period of abnormally increased drive/restlessness, markedly decreased need for sleep (3–4 hours for several nights without feeling tired), and inflated confidence/grandiose business plans, which supports a bipolar spectrum illness rather than unipolar depression, adjustment disorder, or primary anxiety. Given the limited characterization of polarity subtype, unspecified bipolar disorder is the best fit among the candidates.
